"They should receive him not with roses and applause, but with bombs and booby-traps." Gadahn, a California native who calls himself an “American jihadist,” had also appeared in footage released in September 2006. The new 50-minute recording, titled “An Invitation to Reflection and Repentance,” was issued by As Sahab, al Qaeda’s media-production operation. CNN obtained it from LauraMansfield.com, a website focused on terrorism analysis.

In the recording, Gadahn says he is rejecting his citizenship in protest over the incarceration of several people. Among them are Sheikh Omar Abdul Rahman, the blind Egyptian Muslim cleric serving life in prison for his involvement in the 1993 World Trade Center attack, and John Walker Lindh, the so-called American Taliban captured in Afghanistan in 2001.

After holding his passport up to the camera, Gadahn rips it into two pieces. He then tells viewers not to become overly excited because, he claims, he does not require the document to travel.

In a written statement to CNN, Johndroe said the comments reflected an al Qaeda worldview centered solely on violence and death. He added that Bush would go to the region to support mainstream governments seeking freedom and justice for their citizens.

Gadahn, who also uses the name Azzam the American, is listed among the FBI’s Most Wanted. Authorities are offering as much as $1 million for information resulting in his capture.

In 2006, he was indicted for treason and for providing material support to terrorism. He was the first U.S. citizen to face a treason charge since World War II.

Raised in a rural part of California, Gadahn converted to Islam during the mid-1990s and later relocated to Pakistan. Since October 2004, he has appeared in no fewer than eight al Qaeda videos, speaking in English and expressing support for the terrorist organization.
